set.body:
Why
Prior spikes found durable JVM Vector API candidates in extrema and selected integer reductions, while addition and other attractive cases failed portability or allocation gates. SIMD should be promoted only where it survives the real public court and multiple architectures.

Scope
- Re-evaluate only evidence-backed candidates: extrema, Int sum and product, Long sum, and comparison or predicate loops whose scalar specialization still leaves a material gap.
- Test supported JDK baselines, AArch64 and x86_64, small and large thresholds, unaligned tails, NaN and infinity semantics, and the scalar fallback.
- Keep the provider optional and outside shared core. Loading Ravel must not require incubator modules or Vector classes when the provider is absent.
- Inspect code shape and allocation; do not accept a microkernel win that loses through public dispatch, conversion, or module setup. Long product remains rejected unless new evidence overturns its known loss.

Scala.js impact
Scala.js receives no Vector API path. Shared semantics and scalar kernels remain authoritative, full-linked JS output must be unchanged, and no JVM provider type may leak into crossProject APIs. Any shared restructuring must independently demonstrate neutral or positive Node performance.

Acceptance
- Each candidate has public JMH receipts on JDK 21 and 25, AArch64 and x86_64, including scalar fallback and threshold crossings.
- Promotion requires at least 1.20x end-to-end gain in the intended workload class, no semantic drift, no size-proportional temporary allocation, and no unexplained regression above 10 percent.
- Candidates lacking cross-architecture or fallback proof close as explicit no-go decisions rather than entering production.
- JVM and Scala.js gates pass with the provider present and absent where applicable.
set.title: Resolve selective JVM Vector API promotion
